title: Bad inputs are far from their message answer
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic one-way protocol for indexing on $n$-bit inputs, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ be bad for $p$. Then the Hamming distance from $x$ to the answer vector associated with the message sent on $x$ is at least $n/4$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic one-way protocol for indexing on $n$-bit inputs
replaced:
If $x$ is a bad input for $p$, then the Hamming distance from $x$ to the answer vector of its
own message satisfies $d_H\bigl(x, a(\mathrm{send}(x))\bigr) \ge n/4$ (as real numbers).
